title: The Thorn of Highmoor
premise: Cyrus Nystrom has spent twenty-two years in the valley of Highmoor, where an ancient ward suppresses all magic—and hides the beast-speaker gift that would see them executed. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into their hands, Cyrus learns the stranger sold their own soul to the court beneath the mountain to buy Cyrus's childhood safety, and that the debt now falls due. Guided by a sardonic raven named Bramble and hunted by the Warden of Seals, Cyrus must cross a land where every use of their gift draws attention, infiltrate the subterranean court, and steal back the courier's soul before the thirteenth moon turns. In the end, Cyrus discovers the soul can only be freed by offering one in exchange—and chooses to bind their own gift to the mountain rather than let the court claim either soul, returning home changed: no longer hidden, but no longer alone.
about_author: Zephyrine Nakamura is a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to things that could not answer back. They write fantasy about quiet people dragged into loud destinies, and live at the edge of a forest that they insist is listening too.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. We meet Highmoor's magic-dead valley through Cyrus's daily routine—tending goats, speaking wordlessly with animals, hiding the gift even from their adoptive mother Maren. A warded boundary stone hums at the valley's edge. Emotional beat: the ache of belonging somewhere built to erase what you are.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ford
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. During a storm, Cyrus finds a dying woman collapsed at the river ford, her body marked with sigils that shouldn't exist inside the ward. She clutches a leather map case. Emotional beat: fear curdling into reluctant compassion as the woman whispers, 'You're the one I paid for.'

chapters.title: What the Dying Owe
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The stranger, Ilse, dies after pressing the map into Cyrus's hands and gasping about 'the court beneath' and 'thirteen turns.' The map shows a route out of the valley—and a mark over Cyrus's own name. Emotional beat: grief braided with the vertigo of learning your life was purchased.

chapters.title: Maren's Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Maren's flashback reveals she found infant Cyrus at the boundary stone and struck a bargain with Ilse to keep them hidden. Present-day Maren burns Ilse's letter unread. Emotional beat: love expressed as concealment, and its first crack.

chapters.title: Bramble Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A raven named Bramble—who claims to be exiled from the mountain court for theft—reveals he can speak because he crossed the ward long ago. He offers to guide Cyrus if they free his stolen voice as part of the bargain. Emotional beat: wary alliance; first laughter in a darkening story.

chapters.title: Crossing the Stone
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus slips past the boundary stone at night; magic floods back like sound after deafness—their gift roars awake, every creature for miles suddenly audible. Overwhelmed, they nearly turn back. Emotional beat: terror and ecstasy of becoming fully oneself.

chapters.title: The Warden of Seals
chapters.summary: Warden Sable's POV. Introduced hunting Ilse's killer-trail, Sable is revealed as both antagonist and tragic mirror: once a beast-speaker who sold her gift to the court for power. She senses a new speaker crossing the wilds. Emotional beat: cold purpose shadowed by old regret.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Magics
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the trade-town of Vell's Crossing, Cyrus sees how the world prices magic—charms, caged sprites, a soul-broker's stall. They barter a horse-whispering favor for supplies and make their first friend, a sprite-seller named Odji. Emotional beat: wonder undercut by the commodification of everything sacred.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons, Twelve Gone
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV (rendered through Cyrus hearing him). Bramble explains the mechanics: Ilse's soul sits in the court's vault, and when the thirteenth moon fills, it will be consumed to renew the mountain's power. The clock is real and short. Emotional beat: dread made concrete; stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Fens
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Sable catches up; a chase through the marshlands where Cyrus uses their gift to turn a herd of marsh-elk against the Warden—but a fawn dies in the chaos. Emotional beat: first cost of using power; guilt as teacher.

chapters.title: Odji's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odji's POV. Having followed Cyrus, Odji offers passage through the mountain's smuggler tunnels—for a price: Cyrus must speak to the sprite trapped in Odji's lantern and learn why it stays. Emotional beat: tenderness; the theme of freedom versus chosen captivity deepens.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Descending through the smuggler ways, Cyrus glimpses the subterranean court: a glittering, hollow courtiers' hall lit by bottled souls. They witness a ceremony where a soul is 'tasted.' Emotional beat: horror dressed in beauty; corruption made visible.

chapters.title: A Mask Fits Too Well
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. To move through the court, Cyrus disguises themselves as a minor noble's beast-tamer servant—and finds the role seductive: here, their gift earns admiration instead of execution. Emotional beat: temptation of acceptance bought by complicity.

chapters.title: Sable's Offer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable corners Cyrus privately—not to arrest but to recruit. She shows Cyrus the vault and admits she was like them once; the court 'made room' for her. Emotional beat: the antagonist as dark prophecy; loyalty to one's nature versus survival.

chapters.title: The Vault of Kept Voices
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Using Odji's tunnel knowledge and Bramble as scout, Cyrus reaches the vault: shelves of soul-lanterns, each whispering. They find Ilse's—and discover Bramble's voice in a lantern beside it. Emotional beat: heartbreak and resolve; a promise remembered.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Thirteenth Gate
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Odji, exposed as having sold their route to the court months ago under duress, triggers the alarm to save their sister's soul from another shelf. Sable seals the gates. Emotional beat: betrayal born of love, not malice; the trap closes.

chapters.title: The Mountain's Appetite
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Brought before the court's sovereign—a thing wearing the mountain itself like a coat—Cyrus learns the final truth: the court doesn't just keep souls, it eats magic itself, and the valley's dead ward was its first bite. Emotional beat: scale of the threat revealed; despair before defiance.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Will Not Trade
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The sovereign offers Cyrus everything: status, safety, Maren's protection—if they surrender their gift willingly. Cyrus refuses, choosing truth over the comfortable lie they've lived. Emotional beat: the thematic climax of loyalty vs. truth; self-acceptance as weapon.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. Cyrus shatters the vault, freeing every soul—including Bramble's voice and Odji's sister—as Sable, moved by Cyrus's refusal, turns her seals against the court at last. The mountain convulses. Emotional beat: cathartic eruption; enemies becoming allies in the breaking.

chapters.title: The Price Beneath the Moon
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The collapsing court demands a soul to seal its hunger or it will take the whole valley. Cyrus binds their gift—not surrendering it, but anchoring it into the mountain as a living ward, turning the predator into a keeper. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed as transformation, not erasure.

chapters.title: Homecoming Without Hiding
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus returns to Highmoor, gift intact but now shared with the mountain rather than concealed from the world. Maren confesses everything; forgiveness is hard-won but real. Odji and Bramble stay. Emotional beat: reconciliation; love without secrecy at last.

chapters.title: The Fourteenth Moon
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Cyrus's POV. One month on: travelers arrive in Highmoor drawn by rumors of a beast-speaker who tamed a mountain. Cyrus, no longer invisible, greets them openly at the ford where Ilse died. Emotional beat: quiet triumph—the self that was hidden becomes the self that welcomes.
